Usage · {count} icons

What they look like
once they have a job.

A grid of glyphs tells you an icon exists. It does not tell you whether the set holds together on a marketing card, a video thumbnail or a row of settings. Everything below is built from the classes in the README — nothing here is a screenshot.

Marketing cards

The commonest job an icon set ever does. ic-lg ic-primary in a soft tile, one hue for the lot — a feature grid is not the place for six colours.

Drawn from scratch

Nothing traced, nothing re-licensed. The geometry is original, which is what lets the set ship MIT without inheriting anyone's attribution clause.

Five weights, one path

Every weight is generated from the same geometry, so bold cannot drift away from line the way two hand-drawn files always eventually do.

Motion included

Six animations, each with an in, an out and a loop. The draw needs no JavaScript — the build stamps a normalised path length so one CSS rule animates all of them.

Colour that follows yours

Every token reads your design system's --accent first and falls back to ours. Repoint one line and the icons rebrand with everything else.

No dependencies

A sprite, a stylesheet and a JSON index. Nothing to install, nothing to build, nothing that can go stale in a lockfile.

Enforced, not described

Every rule in STYLE.md is a number, and the build fails when an icon breaks one. A style guide that is not executable is a wish.

Thumbnails and the scanline

The scanline's real job. ic-scan ic-tv-loop over a filled icon reads as a screen, which is exactly what a video tile is — and the record dot marks the one that is live.

Drawing the set 12:04 Live Frame & Signal 8:20 On the grid 31:57 Losing lock 4:11 ic-rgb

Sections that draw themselves in

The class is added when the row enters the viewport, so the stroke draws on arrival instead of on load. ic-draw-in with a per-step --ic-delay. Scroll it past and back to replay.

    Take the sprite

    One request for the whole set, or the npm package if you would rather have the source files.

  2. 02

    Point it at your accent

    The colour tokens read --accent before their own fallback, so the set adopts whatever you already have.

  3. 03

    Ship it

    No build step, no runtime, nothing to keep in a lockfile. It is a stylesheet and an SVG.

Interface

Where the set spends most of its life, and the reason the stroke does not scale with the size: at 16px beside a label an icon has to sit, not shout. ic-sm ic-inline.
